gen-fs-quilon-gf-lexend-mega: Editorial confidence lives in Quilon, its strokes thickening and thinning gently. Lexend Mega, a sans drawn as if with one nib, sits beside it like a plain-spoken friend next to a showman.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-lexend-peta: Editorial swagger up top, then a body with wide-mouthed curves and no thinning at all: Quilon leads, Lexend Peta settles in. Quilon is best at drama; Lexend Peta is best at plain legibility.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-lexend-tera: Quilon carries stems a little heavier than their hairlines, giving the heading editorial pull above the plotter-pen lines of Lexend Tera. Shaded strokes meet unshaded ones, and that is the whole story.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-lexend-zetta: Approachable is how Lexend Zetta reads, with ribbon-like strokes of constant width and widely tracked, tall-bodied small letters. And Quilon earns its keep big and short, where its editorial, commanding swing in stroke can show.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-liter: A shimmer of weight up top, then dead-level lines below. Over pages of text, Liter, with no stroke contrast and wide-mouthed rounds, would read smoothly under the commanding Quilon.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-mada: Quilon brings softly varied strokes and an editorial, commanding manner that holds a headline well. But Mada does its best work lower down, with curves that refuse to close and a towering midzone.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-martel-sans: Commanding up front, Quilon moves in a calm ebb and flow of stroke. Martel Sans carries the text with generous curve openings and a high mean line, so paragraphs of it feel light and unhurried.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-matangi: Contemporary lines from Matangi look like twine pressed flat, set against the robust downstrokes and slender turns of Quilon. That hefty lowercase makes running text feel sturdy, smooth and unbroken.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-maven-pro: A gentle ebb and flow of stroke thickness gives Quilon its editorial, commanding voice. Maven Pro keeps joins no thinner than its stems, and that quiet gap in approach is what makes the pair work.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-michroma: Professional in manner, Michroma gives each letter a wide berth, with a tall-bodied lowercase and stubby ascender tips. And Quilon, whose weight shifts noticeably but never dramatically, is worth giving more size than the body.
